name: Riesling
note: High acid, low alcohol, dry to sweet: the fire code and the pork lover. Mosel for feather, Alsace for muscle.

name: Pinot Noir
note: Silk, cherry, forest floor: the red that crosses to fish and worships duck. Burgundy is the reference.

name: Cabernet
note: Cassis and structure: tannin built for seared beef and lamb; never near chile or delicate fish.

name: Malbec
note: Argentina’s velvet power: grilled beef’s constitutional partner; violets over char.

name: Syrah
note: Black pepper, olive, smoked meat: the braise and barbecue intellectual; Rhône savor.

name: Chardonnay
note: Chablis steel to Meursault cream: match the oak level to the butter level.

name: Sauvignon Blanc
note: Grass, gooseberry, cut lime, the vegetable and goat-cheese whisperer.

name: Albariño
note: Sea-spray salinity and white peach, shellfish’s Atlantic soulmate.

name: Chianti
note: Sour cherry and tomato-leaf acid: pasta, pizza, and bistecca by regional law.

name: Barbera
note: Chianti’s juicier cousin: high acid, low tannin, weeknight Italian everything.

name: Champagne
note: Acid plus bubbles: scrubs salt, fat, and fry; the universal rescue and the oyster’s crown.

name: Muscadet
note: Bone-dry, saline, lees-creamy — the oyster wine, priced like a secret.

name: Chablis
note: Unoaked Chardonnay on old seabeds, oyster shell in a glass.

name: Gewürztraminer
note: Lychee and rose, off-dry: aromatic armor for spice and coconut curries.

name: Sake
note: Amino-rich and gentle: umami’s bridge to dashi, soy, and sashimi.

name: Lager
note: Cold, clean, carbonated: fire’s honest antidote and fried food’s friend.

name: Stout
note: Roast and cream — oysters’ old flame and chocolate’s dark mirror.

name: Saison
note: Farmhouse spice and dry finish: charcuterie, pork, and picnic tables.

name: Fino sherry
note: Bone-dry, saline, almond — tapas, consommé, and anything from the sea.

name: Port
note: Fortified depth: blue cheese and chocolate’s appointed hour.

name: Sauternes
note: Botrytis honey and acid: foie, blue cheese, and custard desserts.

name: Rosé
note: Provence’s dry pink: the apéritif hour and the fried-food alliance.
